overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: it took reasonable crowd accommodations, found no racial exclusion, and the chair may limit public participation. It recommended better hallway viewing for future crowds.

allegations.summary: Members of the public, some denied entry to a full meeting room, allege the Board did not adequately accommodate an anticipated crowd at its August 13, 2015 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board took reasonable steps to accommodate an anticipated crowd under the circumstances and in accordance with our general guidance to public bodies.

allegations.summary: Complainants allege the Board specifically excluded a group opposing a project, mostly people of color, from the meeting based on race.
allegations.key_passage: We appreciate that the complainants felt unfairly excluded when other people were let into the meeting; however, we find no evidence that the Board specifically excluded anyone from its meeting based on race.

allegations.summary: Complainants allege the Board refused public comment on the project discussed and did not let the public submit written petitions in opposition.
allegations.key_passage: It is within the Chair's discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, and thus he did not violate the Open Meeting Law by doing so here.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
